title: The format page says how records are kept, then indexes kinds, relations and checks
statement: The format page (`/format`) MUST say how records are kept, then show an index: the kinds by stage, the relations with their words read both ways, and the checks under Errors and Warnings. Kinds and checks MUST be clickable rows leading to their pages.

title: Format pages open in the workbench, with the side bar showing the facts
statement: Each format page MUST open as any other page does: one pane with the page's title in it, and the side bar beside it (a bottom sheet on a phone) showing the kind's or the check's facts, shown and hidden with the same toggle and command as on a record page.

title: A kind page shows everything the reference says about the kind, with a real example
statement: A kind's page (`/format/kinds/<kind>`) MUST show its description; its stage; its allowed parents and children as links to their kind pages; its columns, each with its type, whether it is required, its meaning and its own anchor; its obligation, its ID pattern and its ID scope; the relations out of it and into it by their readable labels, each naming the kind at the other end; and the checks that concern it. It MUST show the product's first record of the kind with a link to it, and the count of the product's records of the kind, with a row per parent leading to that parent's group of them.

title: Every kind and every check has one page, from the product's own data
statement: The kinds, relations, folders and checks the reference pages show MUST be the product's own: the schema with its product kinds, and Lathe's check rows with the product's. The pages MUST be built from the loaded data; a check that reports problems but has no row is the engine's own, listed without an explanation. Each kind MUST have one page at `/format/kinds/<kind>` and each check one page at `/format/checks/<check>`, named by the kind's or check's name as records and problems carry it. A name the format does not know MUST say so, with a link to the format page.

title: A check page shows its explanation, its query and the problems it reports now
statement: A check's page (`/format/checks/<check>`) MUST show its severity, its summary and explanation (rendered Markdown), where it comes from and its query, the kinds it concerns, and the current space's problems with that code as clickable rows.

title: A space's Checks page lists its product's problems, errors first, grouped by check
statement: A space's Checks page MUST list every problem of its product, errors before warnings, grouped by check, each linking to its record, then the problems that belong to no product (data the store refuses, a check that could not run) under a Workspace heading, which every space's Checks page shows. It MUST NOT list another product's problems.

title: A problem's code leads to its check
statement: Wherever a problem's check code is shown, on the Checks page and on a record's page, it MUST be a link to that check's page.

title: Each space has its own Checks page
statement: Each space MUST have its own Checks page, inside the space at its product's ID (`/<product-id>/checks`), opened from the nav's Tools and by the Checks shortcuts; there MUST be no Checks page for every product at once.

title: The product page shows each domain with its coverage
statement: The product page MUST show each domain as a card, linking to the domain page, with one group of small bars per obligation kind the engine reports for it, labeled with the kind's label and in the engine's order, each with designed, built, proved and not-automated-yet counts. It MUST NOT name obligation kinds of its own, and a count the engine does not report MUST NOT be shown as zero.

title: The product page lists its open questions and problems
statement: The product page MUST list the product's open questions, with their owners, and the problems found in its records.

title: The product page sums up what Lathe counts across the product
statement: The product page MUST show, in a Summary section, what Lathe counts across the product's domains: designed, built and proved, totaled over every obligation kind; the not-automated-yet count on its own line, apart from proved; a Tests row totaling its domains' tests by state; its open questions; and its errors and warnings. A product with nothing to count MUST show zeros, not an empty section.

title: Each domain card shows its tests by state
statement: Each domain card MUST show the domain's tests by state under its bars, such as `Tests 12 automated, 1 manual, 2 not automated yet`, from `Coverage.tests`.

title: An open page loads the data again when it changes, at the same address
statement: When the server sends `spec:changed`, an open page MUST load the data again without a manual refresh, staying at the same address.
group_name: Workbench

title: A gap between panels resizes them by drag or keyboard
statement: Each gap between two panels MUST resize them when dragged, and when focused MUST step with the arrow keys (bigger steps with Shift) and jump to the limits with Home and End, the arrow toward a panel growing it. Each size MUST stay within its limits: the navigation 256 to 560 px, the side bar 260 to 640 px, and each pane 20 to 80 percent of the two panes beside a gap, and never narrower than 220 px.
group_name: Workbench

title: Sizes are remembered, and double-click resets one
statement: Each panel's size MUST be remembered across visits (each pane's as a fraction of the panes' width, so it holds whichever panes are open), a remembered size outside its limits MUST fall back to the default, and double-clicking a gap MUST reset its size to the default (navigation 304 px, side bar 340 px), or for a gap between two panes share their space evenly.
group_name: Workbench

title: Dragging the navigation or the side bar small folds it
statement: Dragging the navigation below 180 px MUST fold it to its rail, and dragging the side bar below 160 px MUST hide it; dragging the rail's gap out again MUST unfold the navigation. On a narrow screen there MUST be no gaps to drag: the navigation and the side bar are sheets.
group_name: Workbench

title: Hiding a panel gives its space away and loses nothing
statement: Hiding the nav or the side bar MUST give its space to the main view and MUST keep a control that brings it back: the nav keeps its rail, and the side bar's toggle sits in the page panel's top-right corner, as VS Code's layout toggles do, never as a full-height strip. The side bar MUST describe the same page whichever view is open, so hiding a pane never hides the record's facts for good.
group_name: Workbench

title: A theme applies at once and before first paint
statement: Choosing a theme or a mode MUST apply at once, without a reload. On load, the chosen theme and mode MUST be on the page before the first paint, so it never flashes another theme.
group_name: Workbench

title: One keymap table drives the keys, the palette and the sheet
statement: Every keyboard command MUST be one row in one table (command id, title, group, default keys, where it applies), and the key handlers, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST all be drawn from it, so nothing is listed twice. "Mod" MUST mean Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere, in matching and in what the app shows (⌘⇧P on a Mac, Ctrl+Shift+P elsewhere).
group_name: Keyboard

title: The default shortcuts follow VS Code
statement: The defaults MUST be: Cmd/Ctrl+P and Cmd/Ctrl+K quick open; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P the command palette; Cmd/Ctrl+B the nav; Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+B the side bar; Ctrl+W (Alt+W off a Mac) or Ctrl+1, Ctrl+G (Alt+G) or Ctrl+2, and Ctrl+M (Alt+M) or Ctrl+4 the Wiki, Graph and Model views on and off; Ctrl+3 the focused pane alone (full screen) and back, with Escape to leave it; Ctrl+- and Ctrl+Shift+- back and forward (Alt+Left and Alt+Right left to the browser); F12 open the focused link's record; Shift+F12 the incoming links in the side bar; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M Checks; F8 and Shift+F8 the next and previous problem on the page; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E focus the nav; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+I or Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+I focus the side bar; `/` the nearest search box; `?` and Cmd/Ctrl+/ the shortcuts sheet; in the graph `+` and `-` depth, `t` trace mode, `v` the next of the Tree, Nested and Voronoi layouts, `.` fit, the arrow keys to step through the tree (`LA-V93-R19`) and Enter to focus the box with keyboard focus; and `g` then `c`, `f` or `h` for Checks, the format and home, with a small hint while the second key is awaited.
group_name: Keyboard

title: Shortcuts never get in the way of typing or of the browser
statement: Single-key shortcuts MUST NOT fire while typing; the app MUST call preventDefault only for keys it handles (so Cmd/Ctrl+P never opens the print dialog, and unhandled keys reach the browser); and no binding MUST take a browser essential. A shortcut without Ctrl, Cmd or Alt (a letter, a symbol, a sequence such as `g c`) MUST NOT fire while focus is in a text input, a text area, a select or editable text. Alt+Left and Alt+Right still go back and forward.
group_name: Keyboard

title: A person can change the bindings
statement: The app MUST read optional overrides from local storage (`lathe:keybindings`, a JSON map of command id to a binding or a list of bindings), ignore unknown commands and bad values, and say how in the shortcuts sheet, with each command's id shown.
group_name: Keyboard

title: Every command works without a mouse and is announced
statement: Every command MUST be reachable from the keyboard, and a command that changes the view (a view switch, a panel shown or hidden, full screen, the next problem) MUST be announced to screen readers through a polite live region.
group_name: Keyboard

title: A command's keys suit the platform
statement: A command MAY have other keys off a Mac. On a Mac, Ctrl means the Control key, so Ctrl+W leaves Cmd+W to the browser; elsewhere Ctrl+W closes the tab and Ctrl+G finds the next match, so the view toggles take Alt+W, Alt+G and Alt+M there. A binding that is reserved for the browser on the current platform MUST never be offered, even through an override, and tooltips, `aria-keyshortcuts`, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST show the keys for the current platform.
group_name: Keyboard

title: A tooltip shows the control and its keys
statement: Every icon button and control that has a shortcut MUST show it in its tooltip as its name then its keys ("Show or hide the navigation ⌘B", or "Ctrl+B" off a Mac), after a short hover delay and at once on keyboard focus.
group_name: Keyboard

title: A control with a shortcut has aria-keyshortcuts
statement: Every control with a shortcut MUST carry `aria-keyshortcuts` with its keys.
group_name: Keyboard

title: Every hint reads from the keymap
statement: Every shortcut hint (tooltip, palette row, sheet row, `aria-keyshortcuts`, placeholder) MUST be read from the one keymap with the person's overrides applied, so a rebinding changes every hint; no hint is written by hand.
group_name: Keyboard

title: A tooltip never gets in the way
statement: At most one tooltip MUST show at a time; a click or a page moving focus on load MUST NOT open one; Escape, leaving the control or moving focus away MUST close it.
group_name: Keyboard

title: Below 900 px wide the app has a compact top bar and fits the screen
statement: Below 900 px wide the app MUST take its phone layout. Its top bar MUST hold the menu button, the page's title on one line (cut with an ellipsis) under a link one step up (to the record's parent, a domain's product, or all products, keeping the view in front), and a quick find button. The layout MUST fill the screen's dynamic height (`100dvh`), keep its bars and sheets clear of the safe areas (`env(safe-area-inset-*)`, with `viewport-fit=cover`), and no page MUST scroll sideways at 320 px wide.
group_name: Phone

title: A phone shows one view at a time, switched from the page bar
statement: On a phone a record, group, product or domain page MUST show one view at a time, full width, with no pane headers and no resize handles: the first of the views the address names. The page bar MUST sit under the top bar, compact: the Open pages button, the View switch (Wiki, Graph and Model where offered, one pressed) and the side bar toggle. Switching MUST show that view alone, name it in the address (`?view=graph`) and keep it in the tab, and MUST leave the views remembered for a wide screen alone. The views a page has open on a wide screen are not lost by reading it on a phone.
group_name: Phone

title: The nav is a full-screen sheet with the same rows, sized for a thumb
statement: On a phone the nav MUST open from the top bar's menu button as a full-screen sheet that slides in from the left, keeps the space rail, takes focus to its quick find, keeps Tab inside it, and closes by Escape, its close button or choosing a page, giving focus back to the menu button. Its rows MUST be the wide screen's rows (`LA-V90-R03`), at least 44 px tall on a touch screen, with the fold chevrons as large targets.
group_name: Phone

title: The side bar is a bottom sheet at half or full height
statement: On a phone the side bar MUST open from the page bar as a bottom sheet with a grab handle, at half the screen's height. Dragging the handle up or tapping it MUST take it to full height; dragging it down MUST take it back to half, or close it from half; a flick MUST count as a long drag. Escape, a tap on the dimmed page above it or its close button MUST close it. It MUST take focus as it opens, keep Tab inside it, and give focus back to its toggle when it closes.
group_name: Phone

title: The open pages are a sheet
statement: On a phone the tabs MUST fold into an Open pages button in the page bar that shows how many are open and opens them as a bottom sheet: one row per tab with its ID and title, the active one marked, the preview's title in italics with a Keep button, and a close button on every row. Choosing a row MUST go to that page and close the sheet.
group_name: Phone

title: Quick find and the command palette fill the screen
statement: On a phone quick find MUST open from the top bar (and from its shortcut) as a full-screen sheet: the search box at the top with a Close button, the results as a list under it, more of them than in the dropdown. Choosing a result MUST go there and close the sheet; Escape or Close MUST close it and give focus back. The command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST fill the screen too.
group_name: Phone

title: The graph and the ERD pan, pinch and take taps
statement: The graph and the ERD MUST pan with a finger and zoom with a pinch. On a touch screen a first tap on a node MUST select it: the node is outlined and a card at the bottom of the canvas shows its kind and name with an Open chip; a second tap on it, or the chip, MUST open it; a tap on the empty canvas MUST let it go. A click with a mouse MUST still open a node at once. A long press does nothing of its own: the tap's card is the preview.
group_name: Phone

title: Pages are readable on a phone
statement: On a phone body text MUST be at least 16 px, and every text box MUST be 16 px so the phone does not zoom in on focus. Long IDs MUST wrap rather than widen the page; wide tables and code blocks MUST scroll sideways inside their own box; long lists MUST keep their ten rows with a search (`LA-TRC-SP02`). A record row MUST stack: its ID on a line of its own, its title under it at the row's full width, and its meta (counts, tags, marks) below, so a title is never squeezed beside an ID.
group_name: Phone

title: The browser chrome follows the theme, and sheets move only when motion is welcome
statement: The page MUST carry a `theme-color` meta that follows the theme's sheet color, in light and dark and for any theme chosen. Sheets MUST slide in with the shared motion tokens and MUST appear at once when the system asks for reduced motion (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R04`).
group_name: Phone

title: A tablet in landscape keeps the workbench, sized for touch
statement: The screen's width MUST decide the layout and the pointer the size of targets: at 900 px and wider, a tablet MUST keep the workbench (nav, panes, side bar), with every target at least 44 × 44 px on a touch screen (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07`); below 900 px, a tablet in portrait MUST take the phone layout.
group_name: Phone

title: The first load shifts nothing
statement: When a product, domain or record page first loads, nothing already drawn MAY move: content that arrives late (the specs, the fonts) MUST take room kept for it or appear without pushing what is drawn. The nav draws its lists once the specs have arrived; the fonts are the app's own, preloaded, and a font that is not there in time is not swapped in later.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Moving between records keeps the frame still
statement: Moving to another record through the nav, a link, a graph click, Back or quick find MUST keep the nav, the pane bars and the side bar where they were, and MUST draw the new page at its place from its first frame: a new page at the top, and a page reached by Back or Forward where it was scrolled. The nav's rows, the View toggles and the tabs' close buttons MUST NOT move: a View toggle the page does not offer keeps its slot, dimmed, and every tab has one width.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Opening, closing and maximizing panes moves only the panes
statement: Opening or closing the Wiki, Graph or Model pane, the side bar, and full screen (Ctrl+3) MUST change only the panes' widths: the nav stays, a pane that stays open is not drawn anew, and a canvas that opens appears already fitted.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Folding moves only what is below the row
statement: Opening or closing a row, and Expand all or Collapse all, MUST move only what is below the row or the list; the row itself, the lists above it and the page title stay, and nothing jumps and then corrects.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Resizing follows the pointer
statement: Dragging a gap MUST resize what sits beside it with the pointer and never jump back to a size it left; folding a panel by drag moves nothing on the far side of the page.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: The graph and the Model view keep their canvas still
statement: Re-centering the graph at any depth, changing the depth, and moving between a domain's, an aggregate's and an entity's ERD MUST keep the pane title, the header and the canvas at one size and place; only the boxes and the camera move, on the shared motion.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: A live reload keeps what is in view
statement: When the specs reload while the Reader is scrolled part-way down, what was at the top of the view MUST stay there, and the graph MUST NOT be drawn anew.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Overlays are placed before they show
statement: A tooltip, quick find, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST be placed before they show and stay where they showed; typing in their search box filters the list under it without moving the box.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Switching theme moves nothing
statement: Switching the theme MUST change colors only: no box moves or changes size.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: The mobile sheets move nothing behind them
statement: At phone width (375 px), opening and closing the nav and side bar sheets MUST NOT move the page behind them.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Moving around answers within the performance budgets
statement: Opening a record page, switching views and re-centering the graph MUST answer within the app's performance budgets (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11`): the page is interactive within 1.5 s, a view switch takes under 100 ms of main-thread work, and a re-center at depth 3 glides at 60 Hz, with at most 3 frames over 20 ms and none of 100 ms or more, so the shared motion keeps gliding while the new picture arrives.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: The frame of a page holds still
statement: The nav, the pane bars, the pane titles, the canvases and the side bar MUST keep their place and size unless the Reader moves or resizes them; a change of page changes what they show, not where they are. Content that arrives after the page is drawn (the specs, the fonts, what the graph tells the side bar) MUST take room kept for it, arrive before paint, or be drawn where it pushes nothing the Reader can see.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: A bar keeps one height, and a scroll box its gutter
statement: A bar above content that must not move (a pane title above a canvas, the graph's trail and toolbar, the Model view's caption and key) MUST have a fixed block size, or be one line cut with an ellipsis whose whole text is its tooltip, and text that changes in it MUST be one text, so a new number never moves what follows. A box that scrolls up and down MUST keep room for its scrollbar (`scrollbar-gutter: stable`), so its content keeps its width when the scrollbar comes and goes.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Every page passes the audit
statement: The product, domain, record and group pages, the graph and the Model view, Checks, Format and Appearance, quick find, the command palette, the shortcuts sheet, a tooltip, the side bar and the phone's sheets MUST pass axe-core's WCAG 2.2 AA rules, at 1440 px and at 375 px, in the Lathe theme and the High contrast theme, each in light and in dark.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: Every control is reached and worked by the keyboard
statement: Tab and Shift+Tab MUST reach every control a page draws, each with a visible focus ring, and go all the way round the page and back without being held anywhere. Inside a group of controls (the tab strip, a tree's rows) the arrow keys move and Enter or Space acts; in the graph, Tab moves between the boxes and the arrow keys step through the tree (`LA-V93-R19`). The main tasks MUST work by keyboard alone: open a record from the nav or from quick find, switch views, re-center the graph, fold and unfold a row, show, hide and focus the side bar, and pick a theme.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: Focus lands where the Reader expects
statement: After a move to another page, focus MUST stay on the page, never fall to the body. A control that changes the page in place (a view toggle, the side bar toggle, a fold button) MUST keep focus. Re-centering the graph by keyboard MUST put focus on the box that became the center. A dialog (quick find, the palette, the shortcuts sheet, the theme picker) or a phone sheet (the nav, the side bar, the open pages, quick find) MUST take focus when it opens, keep Tab inside it while it is open, and give focus back to the control that opened it when it closes.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: What changes out of sight is announced
statement: When a command changes the page somewhere other than where focus is (a view opened or closed, the side bar shown or hidden, a theme chosen, every row folded), the app's one announcer (a polite live region) MUST say so in a short sentence, such as "Graph view", "Side bar hidden" or "Color theme: Midnight".
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: A control's name holds its visible text
statement: A control's accessible name MUST contain the text it shows, so a person who says what they see, or hears the name read, finds the same control. Where a control shows a count or a mark, the name is built from what is shown, with words for a screen reader added beside it in hidden text (`sr-only`), rather than an `aria-label` that says something else: the nav's Checks row is named "Checks 3 errors 12 warnings", and a space's button, which shows a monogram the reader is not meant to hear, is named by its product's title in hidden text, with the mark hidden. An `aria-label` that stays MUST include the shown text as a word: "Open pages: 2".
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: No control inside another
statement: A control MUST NOT hold another control: a screen reader reads the outer one as one thing and cannot reach the inner one. Where two act on one item, they sit side by side in a plain wrapper, as a page tab and its close button do.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: A box that scrolls can be reached by keyboard
statement: A box that scrolls on its own and holds nothing that takes focus (a code block, the ERD's key, the shortcuts sheet's groups) MUST take focus itself (`tabindex="0"`) and be named as a region, so the arrow keys can scroll it.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: A target is at least 24 px, or has room around it
statement: On any pointer, a link or control that is not inside a sentence MUST be at least 24 by 24 px, or stand far enough from its neighbors that a 24 px circle on it touches no other target (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.8). Record links listed in a table cell or the side bar are drawn one line tall at 24 px. On a coarse pointer the larger 44 px of `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07` applies.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: Text sits only on the surfaces the theme vouches for
statement: Body text and muted text MUST be drawn only on the surfaces whose contrast every built-in theme guarantees: the page (`--paper`) and a sheet (`--sheet`), which the theme contrast audit (`app/src/theme/audit.ts`) holds to 4.5:1 in light and dark. The shell (`--shell`) is the gap between panels and holds no text: a page that is one panel, such as Checks or Appearance, draws its own `--paper` background rather than let the shell show through.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: The Appearance page lists the themes with previews
statement: `/settings/appearance` MUST list every theme, built in and the reader's own, each with a small preview of the app in its colors and fonts, the one in use marked, and buttons to use it, to duplicate and edit it (built in) or edit it (his own), and to export it. The page MUST be linked from the nav's footer and reachable from the command palette ("Open Appearance settings").

title: A copy of a theme can be edited, renamed, reset and deleted
statement: "Duplicate and edit" MUST make a copy and open it in an editor with: color pickers grouped by purpose (surfaces, text, borders, accent, signals, graph and depth), the light and dark sets side by side; fonts for headings, text and code from a short safe list or a custom font stack; text size, density (comfortable or compact), panel corner radius, gap between panels, and motion (follow the system or always reduced). The theme being edited MUST be the one in use, so the app around the editor is its live preview, beside small light and dark previews. The editor MUST rename the theme, reset it to the built-in it was copied from, and delete it after asking.

title: Hard-to-read colors are flagged while editing
statement: While editing, each text or control color whose contrast on what it is drawn on falls below WCAG AA (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and controls) MUST show a warning beside its swatch, with the ratio, the background and the ratio it needs, for the mode it fails in.

title: Themes are kept per person and travel as files
statement: The reader's own themes, the chosen theme and the mode MUST be kept per person (in the browser's local storage, behind a store the desktop app can replace), and MUST survive a reload. Any theme MUST export as a small, versioned JSON file, and such a file MUST import as a new theme of his own.

title: The Color theme command previews each theme and keeps or puts back
statement: The "Color theme" command (`chooseTheme`, g then t) MUST open a quick pick of every theme. Arrowing to a theme MUST show it on the whole app at once, without keeping it; Enter or a click MUST keep it, and Escape or a click outside MUST put back the theme shown before.

title: Light, dark or system is chosen in the app
statement: Every theme MUST show its light or dark set by the person's choice of System (the default, following `prefers-color-scheme`), Light or Dark. The choice MUST be made by the "Light, dark or system" command (`chooseColorMode`), which previews like the theme picker, and on the Appearance page.

title: A command palette and a shortcuts sheet, both searchable
statement: The command palette MUST list every command that applies on the current page with its shortcut, filter as the person types, and run the chosen one with Enter. The shortcuts sheet MUST list every shortcut grouped as Navigate, View, Graph and Lists, with a search box. Both MUST be dialogs that take focus, keep Tab inside, close with Escape and give focus back.

title: Menus and the palette show each command's keys at the right
statement: The command palette, and any menu, MUST show each command's first shortcut right-aligned on its row in `<kbd>` styling; a command without one shows none.

title: The shortcuts sheet matches the hints
statement: The shortcuts sheet (`?`) MUST list the same keys the hints show, with one "Switch to <product>" row per product that has a key.

title: The record format is a command and a link in the shortcuts sheet
statement: The record format MUST NOT be a link in the nav's footer or rail. It MUST be the "Record format" command in the command palette (g then f) and a link in the shortcuts sheet; the desktop app's Help menu has an entry too. The footer MUST keep saying where the data comes from.

title: The menus are File, Edit, View, Window and Help
statement: The shell MUST have native menus: File (Open Product Folder…, Open Recent, Close Window), Edit, View (the app commands, then Reload, Force Reload, Toggle Developer Tools, the zoom items and Toggle Full Screen), Window, and Help (Record Format, Keyboard Shortcuts), with the app menu first on a Mac.

title: A menu choice runs the app command by its ID
statement: A menu item for an app command MUST send the command's ID from the keymap (such as `viewWiki` or `toggleNav`) to the page, and the app's command system MUST run it, as if its key had been pressed.

title: The menus take no key from the app
statement: App command items MUST carry no accelerator, so every key reaches the app's keymap, with its overrides, unchanged.

title: Open Recent lists the last 10 folders
statement: File › Open Recent MUST list the recent folders, latest first, each opening its folder, then Clear Menu; with none it MUST say No Recent Folders.

title: Settings opens the app's settings in the focused window
statement: Settings… (Cmd+,) MUST open `/settings/appearance` in the focused product window.

title: The window has no system title bar; the app draws its own
statement: A window MUST have no system title bar. The app MUST draw its own 38 px bar across the top of the window, on the shell color (`--shell`) with no border, so the bar and the shell are one surface, and lay the page out under it. On macOS the traffic lights MUST float over the bar's left end, centered in its height; on Windows and Linux the native window controls MUST draw over its right end. The bar MUST leave room for them. The window MUST keep its title and, on macOS, its represented folder, which the Window menu and Mission Control show.

title: Back and forward follow the app's history
statement: The bar MUST start with back and forward buttons that run the app's `goBack` and `goForward` commands. Each MUST be disabled when there is no page to go to in that direction, where the browser can tell.

title: The command center names the page and opens quick find
statement: The bar's center MUST hold a command center: a pill showing the product name and the current page's heading ("Lathe — Add an item to the basket"), centered on the window and cut short with an ellipsis when it does not fit. Clicking it MUST open quick find (`quickOpen`), and its tooltip MUST show the shortcut.

title: The layout toggles show and hide the navigation and the side bar
statement: The bar MUST end with toggle buttons for the navigation and the side bar that run `toggleNav` and `toggleSideBar`, the same commands as the menus and the keys. Each MUST say with `aria-pressed` whether its panel shows, and its tooltip MUST show the shortcut. The side bar toggle MUST be disabled on a page that has no side bar.

title: The bar drags the window, and a double-click zooms it
statement: Dragging the bar anywhere but on a control MUST move the window. Double-clicking it there MUST zoom or maximize the window, as the system's setting says. Its controls MUST take clicks and never drag.

title: The window's chrome follows the theme
statement: When the theme or the light or dark mode changes, including the system's appearance while the mode is System, the app MUST send the theme's shell and ink colors to the shell through `window.latheDesktop.setChrome`. The shell MUST then set the window's background and, on Windows and Linux, the window controls' colors.

title: In a browser there is no title bar
statement: The app MUST draw the title bar only when `window.latheDesktop` is present. In a browser the page MUST stay as it is.

title: A window opens on the shell color with a launch view until the specs answer
statement: A new window MUST show the theme's shell color at once and a launch view (the logo and "Opening <product>…") until the page has the product's specs, with no white flash and no blank window.

title: A folder the engine cannot load gets an error page with a way on
statement: When Lathe cannot start for a folder or the engine cannot load it, the window MUST show the message with Retry, Open Another Folder and Reveal in Finder.

title: A launch, error or About page runs only the buttons it shows
statement: A button press from the shell's own pages MUST run only when it is one of the actions that page shows, and only from that page.

title: About Lathe shows the versions and links to the repo and the record format
statement: About Lathe MUST open a small window with the app's, the engine's and Electron's versions and links to the repo and the record format, opened in the system browser. Check for Updates MUST NOT show until signed builds are published.

title: The app icon reads at every size and in light and dark Docks
statement: The app MUST have an icon drawn on Apple's icon grid, rendered from SVG for macOS (`.icns`, 16 to 1024 px), Windows (`.ico`) and Linux (PNGs), with a bolder drawing at 16 and 32 px. A development build (`npm run dev`) MUST show the icon with a "DEV" band in the Dock.

title: The Dock menu opens a new window and lists recent folders
statement: The Dock menu MUST have New Window, which runs Open Product Folder, and every folder opened MUST be added to the system's recent documents, which macOS lists in the Dock menu.

title: The Dock badge follows the window in front
statement: The badge MUST show the error count of the focused product window, or of the one focused last while another app is in front. A count MUST be a whole number from 0 up, from the window's own page; anything else MUST be ignored.

title: The graph is a view of a page, not a place in the nav
statement: The graph MUST be reached as a view of the page in hand (its Graph view toggle, Ctrl+G or Alt+G, Ctrl+2, the command palette), never as a separate item in the side navigation.

title: A group that is a record links; a group the app computes only folds
statement: A group that is a record (a capability, a use case, an aggregate) MUST link to its page wherever it heads its members; a stage or kind group MUST NOT pose as a record: its nav row only folds and its heading is not a link.

title: A selected row is the whole row
statement: In the nav, as in VS Code's explorer, a row MUST be as wide as the nav panel, indented by padding for its depth rather than by nested margins, with its indent guides and its fold chevron inside it. The current page's row MUST carry the selection over the whole row, from the panel's left edge over the indent and the chevron to its right edge, in the selection tint with its text and chevron in steel, with no bar of its own at its edge. A hovered row MUST take the hover tint over the whole row, and while the nav is used from the keyboard the selected and the focused row MUST show a 1 px steel outline. The lists stay nested for screen readers.

title: The menu lists each product and its domains
statement: The left menu MUST show each product as a space in its rail, and list the current space's domains (with their capabilities) in its panel.

title: The nav collapses to a rail, and is a full-screen sheet on a narrow screen
statement: A toggle MUST collapse the nav to a narrow rail of icons (the logo, Quick find, the spaces, Checks), each with a tooltip and an accessible name, and expand it again; the state MUST be remembered. Under about 900 px wide the nav MUST become a full-screen sheet opened from the menu button in the top bar, with focus moved into it and kept inside it, and closed by Escape, its close button or choosing a page, with focus returned to the menu button.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: The nav folds by section and shows where you are
statement: The Tools section, and each domain and folder of the current space, MUST each fold and unfold with a chevron button carrying `aria-expanded`; the section holding the current page MUST open itself. The current space MUST have no heading of its own, since the rail names it: its first row is its overview. The current page MUST be marked clearly with `aria-current="page"` and scrolled into view. Icons MUST be inline line icons; counts MUST be quiet badges, with errors red and warnings amber on Checks; long names MUST be cut short with the full name as a tooltip; items MUST be at least 32 px high. A footer MUST say where the specs come from (the record format is a command and a link in the shortcuts sheet, as `LA-V65-R71` says).
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: Quick find jumps to anything by ID or title
statement: A search field at the top of the nav MUST find any record, domain or product by ID or title, best matches first (exact ID, ID prefix, title), and MUST let the person move through the results with the arrow keys and open one with Enter.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: The rail lists each product as a space
statement: The nav MUST have a rail about 56 px wide at its far left with one square icon per product in the products' ID order, and no item above every product. Each item MUST name itself in a tooltip.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The current space is marked
statement: The rail MUST mark the current space with an accent bar and `aria-current`.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The nav lists only the current space's things
statement: The nav MUST list the current space's product page, its domains, each folding into its five stages as the schema places kinds (with the capabilities in order under Use cases), and its groups (the product's other kinds of children), and MUST NOT list another product's domains.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: Choosing a space opens the last page visited in it
statement: Choosing a space MUST open the last page visited in that space during the session, or its product page when there is none.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: Alt and a number switch spaces
statement: Alt+1 to Alt+9 (⌥1 to ⌥9 on a Mac) MUST switch to the first nine spaces in rail order, and the command palette MUST offer a "Switch to <product>" command for each, with its keys. Every other shortcut MUST keep working.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: Quick find searches the current space only
statement: Quick find MUST search only the current space's records (and the record format's kinds and checks), as one list for the arrow keys, and MUST NOT list anything of another product: switching product is the rail's job.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The rail stays in the nav sheet on a narrow screen
statement: On a narrow screen the rail MUST stay visible inside the nav sheet.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: No view in a space shows another product
statement: Inside a space the side bar (Details, Outline, History), the graph and its trail and minimap, the Model view, hover cards, the reference's records and its "where the X are" links, saved tabs and the space's last page MUST show only that product, and the desktop Dock badge MUST count only its problems and the workspace's. A link into another product MUST NOT be drawn or listed, and another product's ID named in a text field MUST show as plain text, not as a link.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The nav reads like stage folders
statement: Under the current space, the nav MUST list the product page; then Shared, only when it holds anything, holding the patterns, the standards and the records with no owner; then each domain, which unfolds into its five stages, then its open questions.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: Stages and folders fold one level at a time, with counts
statement: Every domain, stage and folder MUST be a foldable row showing one level when opened; only the level under the space MUST show by default. Each stage and folder MUST show its count of records, and one with no records MUST NOT be listed.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: The current page's branch opens itself
statement: Opening a page from the nav, or on the nav's first draw (a load, a reload, the nav expanded or opened as a drawer), MUST open the nav rows that hold it: a domain page its domain; a record page its domain and stage (or Shared), and the parents above it in that stage; a group page the folder of its kind. A page opened anywhere else (a link in the page, the graph, Back, quick find) MUST leave the nav's rows where they are (`LA-V61-R28`): the closed row that holds the page is marked instead, and opening that row opens the branch down to the page.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: Use cases lists capabilities, then use cases outside any
statement: The Use cases folder MUST list the domain's capabilities in their order, then the use cases outside any capability; a capability's own use cases stay under it. A use case's flow MUST be listed in Interaction design and a requirement's tests in Test plan.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: Layers and test groups fold in the nav, with counts
statement: In the side nav, technical and test kind groups MUST be foldable rows with their counts, one level shown by default, and the current page's branch MUST open itself through its layer or its test groups. a kind group's row MUST only fold. What is folded MUST last for the session.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: Sub-layers nest, and rules under an entity sit under it
statement: Records with no owner MUST be listed in their product's Shared, by stage (value objects and their constraints, views and their requirements, integrations, UI components), and a specification in its domain's Domain model, in the nav and on the domain page alike
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: Quick find finds kinds and checks
statement: Quick find MUST list every kind as "Kind: <label>" and every check as "Check: <name>", found by their names and labels, each leading to its page.

title: A domain has one page, at its ID
statement: A product's and a domain's only page MUST be their overview, at their bare ID (`/LA`, `/LA-EXP`); there MUST NOT be a second, generic record page for them. That one page MUST lose nothing the generic page showed: its text in the wiki, and in the side bar its kind, fields, data file, parent, children, links out and in, and problems.

title: The domain page groups records by stage
statement: The domain page MUST group its records by its five stages, each record under its parent where the parent is of the same stage (an aggregate's invariants, a use case's requirements).
group_name: Find a record in a domain

title: A search box filters records by ID or title
statement: The domain page MUST have a search box that filters the shown records by ID or title as the reader types.
group_name: Find a record in a domain

title: The domain page shows its coverage gaps and problems
statement: The domain page MUST list the domain's coverage gaps (each with the missing link) and the problems about its records.
group_name: Find a record in a domain

title: The domain page and group pages use the same folders as headings
statement: The domain page MUST head its records with the same stages and folders as the nav (the five stages), listing a folder's records directly or under one heading per kind when it holds several, and keeping its one-level-deep folding. A group page MUST name the stage and folder of its kind, such as Interaction design.

title: Technical specification lists layers in order, each with its components
statement: A domain's Technical specification MUST list its records by technical kind, in the plan's order (repositories, data models, tables, value types, predicates, event types, projections, command handlers, query handlers, event handlers, services, endpoint handlers, adapters, then the product's own kinds), each record with the design record it implements
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: Test plan groups tests by family and by what they prove
statement: A domain's Test plan MUST list its tests by test kind in the plan's order (constraint, invariant, specification, policy, domain service, use case, view, endpoint, flow, integration and pattern rule tests), each with its parent and run by
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: The domain page and group pages head the same groups
statement: The domain page MUST head Technical specification's and Test plan's kind groups with the same names and order as the nav, keeping its one-level-deep folding of records and its filter. A group page of tests MUST read them in the same groups.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: APIs and integrations sit in Interaction design, and technical flows in Technical specification
statement: The nav, the domain page and the graph MUST place an endpoint in its domain's Interaction design, and an integration in its product's Shared, by its kind's stage in the meta-model

title: The domain page's coverage shows every obligation kind and the tests by state
statement: The domain page's Coverage section MUST show one group of bars per obligation kind the engine reports, the pattern rule line among them, each with designed, built, proved and not-automated-yet counts, then the domain's tests by state. Its gaps MUST name each obligation, pattern rules included, that the domain does not yet design, build or prove.
group_name: Traceability

title: View and API requirements are listed under their view or endpoint
statement: The domain page MUST list each view requirement and API requirement nested under its view or endpoint, and each record of an obligation kind a product adds under its parent, with its gaps and problems on its row. Searching for one MUST keep its view or endpoint shown above it.
group_name: Traceability

title: Each test shows its state, and one not automated yet never looks like proof
statement: The domain page MUST tag each test with its state. A test not automated yet MUST look unfinished and MUST NOT be counted or drawn as proof.
group_name: Traceability

title: A domain page lists the patterns it follows
statement: A domain page MUST have a Patterns we follow section listing each pattern that the domain itself follows ("followed by the whole domain", with every rule applying) or that any of its use cases follows, with the use cases that follow it. Each pattern's rules MUST be folded under its row, one level deep like the rest of the page, and each rule MUST show whether this domain proves it (its pattern rule test naming the domain is automated or manual), with a test not automated yet shown apart, worked out as the engine counts it (LA-TRC-SP04). A domain that follows no pattern MUST say so.
group_name: Traceability

title: A rule the domain marks not applicable says so, with the use case and reason
statement: When a pattern rule names a setting and every use case in the domain that follows the pattern gives that setting a not-applicable reason, the rule MUST show as not applicable in that domain instead of its proof, naming each use case (as a link) and its reason.
group_name: Traceability

title: A waived rule says Waived here, with the value the domain gives
statement: Where a pattern rule is waived in a domain, the domain page, the pattern page and the pattern rule page MUST show it there as "Waived here: <setting> is <value>", naming the value or values that domain's followers give the setting (or "not given"), instead of its proof, and the rule's Traceability gaps MUST leave that domain out. A rule's row MUST say what it applies when.
group_name: Traceability

title: Every record ID shown is a link to that record
statement: Wherever a page shows a record ID, it MUST be a real link (`<a href>`) to that record's page, so any reference can be followed or opened in a new tab.

title: A wiki page shows one level below its record by default
statement: A wiki page (product, domain, record or group) and the side bar MUST show by default only the records one level below the page's own record. Anything deeper MUST be folded under its row and open only when the person opens it, opens everything, or searches for something inside it.

title: A folded row keeps its count and its marks
statement: A folded row MUST still show how many records it holds ("4 requirements") and its own coverage marks and problem badge, so nothing hidden is forgotten.

title: A record ID named in text is a link in the text, never a relation
statement: A record ID named in a text field MUST be shown only as a link in the text: it MUST NOT appear among the record's links out or in, in the graph, or in coverage.

title: Code and links in text are shown as written
statement: Turning named IDs into links MUST NOT change text inside code blocks, links the author wrote, or code spans holding anything besides one ID; a code span holding one lone record ID is wrapped in the link with its code style kept, and it MUST run only on the sanitized HTML.

title: A row that leads to one record is one link to it
statement: A list row that leads to one record MUST hold exactly one link that stands for the whole row, and that link MUST be a real link (`<a href>`) to the record's page, so the row can be followed or opened in a new tab like any other reference. Other links in the row lead elsewhere and stay links of their own.

title: Links are shown by their labels, never by relation codes
statement: Wherever a page names a link, as a heading, a list title, a field label, an edge label or a tooltip, it MUST use the relation rule's `forward_label` read from the link's source or its `reverse_label` read from its target. A relation code such as `fulfills` or `hears` MUST NOT be shown as a heading or label; it may appear only as code, where a page explains how to write a link.

title: A page changes data only through its record actions
statement: A page MUST change a record only when the person acts on one of its record actions (Edit, Add or Remove), and then only by sending one write to `POST /api/write`, which the store's command layer applies or refuses whole. Opening, reading or searching a page MUST NOT send a write, and no page MUST write a data file itself, so every change is one the schema accepts and is reviewed in git.

title: A list of one kind is titled by that kind, through plural()
statement: A list of a record's children or a group's members MUST be titled by its kind's plural label, through `plural()`, when it holds one kind ("Invariants", "UC requirements", "Components"), and MUST be titled "Children" or "Members" only when it holds more than one kind to tell apart. Its count stays beside the title, and its accessible name and search box follow the title ("Invariants of LA-EXP-A1", "Filter domain rules"). A group's label MUST read as plain English, and any kind it names MUST come from the workspace's kind labels through `plural()`, such as "Command handlers", so a product that renames a kind sees its own name.

title: A refused change shows its reasons in place and changes nothing
statement: When the store refuses a write, the form or question MUST stay open with what the person entered, show every reason the store gave beside the input or section its command came from, and take focus to the reasons. Nothing on the page, and no data file, MUST change.

title: Steps are shown in their positions, as numbers
statement: A flow's steps MUST be shown in their `position`, compared as numbers (so step 10 comes after step 2), then by ID; the store refuses a step without a whole-number position, so none is ever hidden.

title: A step is always shown under its flow
statement: Wherever steps are shown, on a page or in the graph, each MUST be shown under the flow it belongs to, never as a record apart from it.

title: The record page shows the whole record, field by field
statement: The record page MUST show the record's ID, kind and title; its text fields (a statement, a goal, a description, a test's Given, When and Then, notes) rendered as Markdown, a test's three as one scenario; its part rows laid out (an entity's or event's fields as a table, a flow's steps in order, a product's roles, a table's keys); its other columns as facts; and its parent and children.
group_name: Follow a record's links

title: The record page shows links both ways, grouped by relation
statement: The record page MUST show the record's outgoing links and its incoming links, each grouped by relation, with every linked record clickable.
group_name: Follow a record's links

title: A record's text is sanitized before it is shown
statement: The HTML rendered from a record's text fields MUST be sanitized before it is put on the page, because records are written by agents as well as people.
group_name: Follow a record's links

title: The record page shows the problems about it
statement: The record page MUST list every problem whose record is this one.
group_name: Follow a record's links

title: Anywhere on a record's row opens that record
statement: In every list of records (the rows of a product, domain, record or group page, the side bar's children and members, coverage gaps, open questions, what a requirement fulfills, the patterns a domain follows, and the problems on the checks page), a click anywhere on a row MUST open the record the row leads to, not only a click on its ID or title. Cmd/Ctrl-click and middle-click MUST open it in a new tab. The row's other controls (its fold chevron, other record links, badges and buttons) MUST keep doing what they do. Keyboard focus stays on the row's one link, and its focus ring and hover cover the whole row; a tree's arrow keys work as before.
group_name: Follow a record's links

title: Record IDs named in text are links
statement: In a record's rendered text fields (a record page, and a product's or domain's overview), every ID-shaped token that is the ID of a record of the space, other than the record itself, MUST become a link to the record's address, its bare ID (`/<id>`), with the record's title on hover, and a plain click MUST move within the app. An ID inside a code block, an existing link or a code span with other text MUST NOT be linked, nor part of a longer ID; a code span holding exactly one such ID MUST link.
group_name: Follow a record's links

title: An ID that names no record stays plain text
statement: An ID-shaped token in a text field that is no record of the space MUST be shown as written, as plain text: it MUST NOT be a link, and nothing reports it, since no check reads text for IDs.
group_name: Follow a record's links

title: Every list that can grow stays at ten rows, in every view
statement: Every list that can grow, including the side bar's lists (raw links, a product's or domain's children, problems, what the graph connects, the files a trace reaches, the outline's rows) and a group page's members, MUST use the long list: ten rows, then a scroll inside with a search box and a count.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: Wiki pages and the side bar open one level deep
statement: A product page MUST list its domains (and its summary and questions) but not their contents; a domain page its direct children grouped by kind (its five stages and open questions, each stage's kinds in the schema's order, and any other kind such as capabilities, in their `position`), each row showing its count of children; a record page its fields, its text, direct children and links; a group page its members. Each row with children MUST have a disclosure button (`aria-expanded`, a chevron) and each section an Expand all / Collapse all button. What is opened MUST be remembered for the session while moving around. A search inside a section MUST reveal matching nested records by opening their row just for the match. Right arrow MUST open a row (or move into it) and Left close it (or move to its parent). The command palette MUST offer Expand all and Collapse all for the page.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: Grouped requirements and rules read under their group headings
statement: The wiki MUST show a record's children that name a group, such as a use case's requirements, a view's view requirements, an endpoint's API requirements, a pattern's rules or a standard's rules, under their group headings: the ungrouped ones first, without a heading, then each group in the order it first appears. A use case's requirement table and a standard's rule table MUST head each group's rows with its name, and the side bar's Outline MUST list the groups.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: A flow's page shows its steps in order as a table
statement: A flow's record page MUST show its steps, when it has any, as a table in step order with the columns Step (order and ID), What happens (the title), Invokes, In view and Fulfills, each linked ID going to its record.
group_name: Read a flow step by step

title: A step's description and linked titles fold under its row
statement: Each step row MUST show one level: the step and the IDs it links to. Its description and …of what it invokes, happens in, exchanges with and fulfills MUST be folded under the row's disclosure, with Expand all and Collapse all for the table.
group_name: Read a flow step by step

title: A step row shows its problems, and a flow without steps shows no table
statement: A step's row MUST carry a badge for its errors or warnings. A flow with no steps MUST NOT show a steps table.
group_name: Read a flow step by step

title: A flow with several paths shows a table per path
statement: When a flow's steps sit on more than one `path` (a step with no path is on the main path), its page MUST show each path as its own table, headed by the path's name, the main path first and then the others by name, each in its own step order, never interleaved by `position` across paths.
group_name: Read a flow step by step

title: An API's page lists its endpoints and the requirements they share
statement: A command's or query's page MUST show the endpoint that exposes it, with its method and route, and an endpoint's page its API requirements, each in its own section with its count
group_name: Read a domain's endpoints and integrations

title: An integration's page lists its exchanges and names its system
statement: An integration's page MUST list the flow steps that exchange with it, in a section with its count, saying which outside system it is when it names one
group_name: Read a domain's endpoints and integrations

title: Every record page has Edit, which opens its form in place
statement: Every record's page MUST offer Edit, Add and Remove as buttons in its record actions. Edit MUST open the record's form in place of the page's content, holding its columns, its parent, its links and its part rows as they are; Save MUST send every change as one write, and Cancel MUST leave the record as it was.
group_name: Change a record on its page

title: Inputs follow the schema, and pickers offer only valid targets
statement: Each input MUST take the type of its column (`LA-EXP-DS12`), an enum as a select of its values; the parent and each link MUST be picked from the records they may name, in the same product, and the form MUST say before it writes when a required input is empty or a value is not of its type.
group_name: Change a record on its page

title: A child is added from its parent's page
statement: Add MUST open an empty form for a record of a kind that may sit under the page's record (a choice of kind when several may), with that record as its parent and the next free ID suggested, and MUST add it in one write.
group_name: Change a record on its page

title: Remove asks first, naming what still references the record
statement: Remove MUST ask first, listing what still references the record (its children, the links into it, other records' rows that name it); while anything does, it MUST say the removal will be refused until those go. Confirming MUST send one write that removes the record with its part rows and the links it starts.
group_name: Change a record on its page

title: A refusal shows inline with its reasons
statement: A write the store refuses MUST show its reasons at the top of the form or question and beside the input each came from (`LA-V92-R10`), in the store's own words without a file and line, and the person MUST be able to fix the input and save again.
group_name: Change a record on its page

title: Editing works from the keyboard and a screen reader
statement: The record actions, the form and the remove question MUST work from the keyboard alone, as the rest of the app does: every input labeled, a required input marked as required, an input with a problem marked invalid and described by its message, focus taken to the form's first input when it opens and back to its action when it closes, and a change announced. They MUST pass the accessibility suite (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R10`) with no finding.
group_name: Change a record on its page

title: A test's page shows its state
statement: The record page MUST show a test's state; for a test not automated yet it MUST look unfinished and say that it does not count as proof.
group_name: Traceability

title: The record content can sit inside another view
statement: A record's content (header, typed fields, parts, parent, children and links) MUST be one piece that takes a record ID and an `onNavigate` callback, apart from the page around it, so the graph can show it beside itself. Links inside it MUST go through `onNavigate` on a plain click and stay real links otherwise. It SHOULD read well at half the screen width.
group_name: Traceability

title: Every list stays at 10 rows and can be searched
statement:
Every list in the spec pages (the menu's domains, a domain's record groups and nested lists, coverage gaps, problems and checks, open questions, a record's children and links both ways) MUST show up to 10 items as a plain list. With more than 10 it MUST show the first 10 rows' height and scroll inside, with a search box above it that filters by ID and title, a count such as "12 of 48", and a clear message when nothing matches.

The search box MUST be reachable with Tab, Escape MUST clear it, and the scrolling area MUST take focus so it scrolls from the keyboard. The list MUST know nothing about specs, so other views can use it.
group_name: Traceability

title: A pattern page shows its settings, rules and followers
statement: A pattern's page (`/<id>`) MUST show a settings table (each setting and the rules that depend on it), its rules, and each domain that follows it with that domain's following use cases, the value each gives for each setting, and the domain's status for each rule as on the domain page. A pattern nobody follows MUST say that no domain owes its rules. The rules MUST NOT be listed a second time as plain children.
group_name: Traceability

title: A pattern rule page shows the domains that owe it
statement: A pattern rule's page MUST list each domain that follows its pattern, with that domain's standing for the rule: proved, not automated yet, not proved, not applicable with the reasons, or waived.
group_name: Traceability

title: An obligation lists what designs, builds and proves it
statement: An obligation's record page MUST show a Traceability section after its text and before its children, with these groups in this order, each left out when empty: Designed by (for a UC requirement the flow steps that fulfill it, for any other obligation the technical record that implements its design, each marked built or not built), Proved by (its tests, each with its state), then its other incoming links under their reverse labels, then its links out under their forward labels. Which links go in which group MUST follow only the schema: the tree, a relation's role, and whether the kind is an obligation. A group is titled by its links' label and holds each record once.
group_name: Traceability

title: Each gap shows as a callout linked to its check
statement: An obligation's Traceability MUST name each gap in a callout, "Not designed yet", "Not built yet" or "Not proved yet", saying when its test is not automated yet, taken from coverage's own gaps for the domain that owes it, never from a count of its own, so it never disagrees with the coverage marks or the checks. Each callout MUST link to the page of the check that reports it (`not-designed`, `not-built`, `not-proved`). A pattern rule MUST show one line for each domain that owes it, judged from that domain's test alone.
group_name: Traceability

title: A use case shows its requirements in a table
statement: A use case's Traceability MUST show a table with one row per UC requirement and the columns Requirement, Designed, Built and Proved, each cell linking the records that design, build or prove it and flagging a gap, followed by its flow and the patterns it follows.
group_name: Traceability

title: A technical record and a test show what they implement, prove and run from
statement: A technical record's Traceability MUST show what it implements, then that record's tests, rolled up, then its other links under their labels. A test's MUST show what it proves (its parent), then its run by: its level, its state, and the file that runs it, flagged when the file is missing, or its manual reason. Any other kind MUST show its links out under their forward labels and its links in under their reverse labels.
group_name: Traceability

title: Domain events show what raises them and what hears them
statement: An aggregate's page MUST list its domain events in their own list titled "Domain events", each row one link to the event saying which commands raise it and how many policies hear it, and its list of other children MUST NOT list them again. An event's page MUST show its fields (its `event_field` rows), as an entity's page shows its fields, and its Traceability MUST list "Raised by" and "Heard by"; a policy MUST list its event under "Hears". Every one of these words MUST come from the relations' labels in the schema.
group_name: Traceability

title: Kinds, problem codes and columns link to their format pages
statement: The side bar's Kind row MUST link to the kind's page, on a record page and on a group page. Every problem's code on the Checks page, the domain page and the record page MUST link to its check's page. A record's column labels MUST link to that column on its kind's page.
group_name: Authoring

title: Standards are listed with the technical specification, each listing its rules and what meets them
statement: The nav MUST list a product's standards in the technical specification stage. A standard's page MUST list its rules in a table, one row each, with what meets each rule, and say when nothing does yet.
group_name: Authoring

title: A standard rule shows what meets it
statement: A standard rule's Traceability MUST list what meets it under Met by, and what meets it MUST list the rule under Meets. The reference MUST have a page for each standard kind, made from the schema.
group_name: Authoring

title: Motion carries no meaning and stops under reduced motion
statement: Motion in the graph MUST only help the eye follow a change: the view after a move MUST be the same with or without it, and when the system asks for reduced motion the camera MUST jump to the new view with no glide.

title: By touch, a tap selects a node and a second tap opens it
statement: A finger has no hover, so on a canvas a first tap on a node MUST select it and say what it is before anything moves, and only a second tap on the same node, or an explicit Open, MUST open it. A pointer that can hover opens a node with one click.

title: A canvas stays mounted and is fitted before it paints
statement: The graph and the Model view MUST keep their canvas mounted while their content changes, MUST fit their first picture before it paints, and MUST NOT cut a glide short by fitting again when their size has not changed.

title: Domain events are drawn in the spark colors
statement: Wherever a domain event is drawn as a node or box in the graph, it MUST be a flag, notched on the right (`LA-V93-R06`), in the `--spark` and `--spark-bg` tokens, and its `raises` and `hears` lines, the `hears` lines dashed MUST be drawn in `--spark`, the `reacts_to` lines dashed, so events read the same in every view.

title: A domain is drawn as a hexagon
statement: In the graph every domain node MUST be drawn as a hexagon, with flat top and bottom edges and pointed left and right ends, drawn as a polygon, not a rotated box. The points' chamfer MUST grow with the node's box scale (12 map units at box scale 1), at most a quarter of its width, so a very tall domain still reads as a hexagon and not as a diamond. Its border MUST follow the outline in every state, hovered, focused, keyboard-focused and selected by a tap, by coloring and thickening the outline's own edge, drawn inside the polygon. A parent line into a domain MUST meet the tip of its point, and a parent line out of one MUST start on its slanted side, where the outline is at the child's middle; a line meets every other shape's outline the same way (`LA-V93-R06`). The minimap draws boxes.

title: Each kind is drawn in a shape of its own
statement:
In the graph every kind MUST have one shape, the same in every view, as a secondary cue after its label, and every shape MUST keep a rectangular footprint so boxes still stack:

| Group | Kind | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | product | a large rounded box |
| | domain | a hexagon (`LA-V93-R05`) |
| | stage and folder groups | a folder with a tab |
| | capability | a slice pointing right |
| Define | aggregate | a double border |
| | entity | a plain box |
| | domain rule, pattern rule | an octagon |
| | domain event | a flag, notched on the right |
| | use case | a stadium |
| | requirement | a page with a folded corner; an interaction requirement too, with a marker |
| | pattern | stacked boxes |
| Design | flow | a chevron bar |
| | flow step, technical step | a chevron |
| | view | a window with a top bar |
| | endpoint | a box with a port notch on its left |
| | API, integration | a plain box with a port mark |
| | layer | a striped box |
| | component | a box with component tabs |
| | test | a shield |
| | technical flow | as a flow, with a gear mark |
| Other | open question | a diamond |
| | standard, standard rule | as a pattern and a pattern rule, with a ruler mark |

A kind a product adds MUST be a plain box. In the Tree view and a trace a box's outline MUST be its kind's shape: a polygon shape drawn with its edge inside the polygon, so its border, hover, focus, keyboard ring and a tap's selection color and thicken the outline itself, and a rounded shape with its border's corners and its rings following them. In the Nested and Voronoi views every box MUST keep its rectangle or cell and show its kind's shape as a small mark before its kind and ID line. A shape's corners and notches MUST grow with its box's scale, at most a share of its side. Its label and problem badge MUST stay inside its shape's safe area, which the map keeps when it wraps and sizes the label, so no line is clipped or crowded by a notch or a corner. Every shape and mark MUST be in the graph's key (`LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R21`). The new kinds take shapes of their own: a value object a pill; constraint, invariant, specification and policy an octagon, with a mark each; a command a box with an arrow notch; a read model a box with rows; a query a box with a lens mark; a domain service a box with a gear mark; a term a tag; a view requirement and an API requirement a page with a folded corner and a marker; technical kinds a box with component tabs (a table a grid); every test kind a shield.

title: The map is drawn on a canvas, anew each frame
statement:
Focusing a node, by a click, the address, Back and Forward, the step keys or the trail, MUST move the camera only: it MUST frame the focus and the levels the depth shows below it to fill the pane, with the parent's level kept in view in a strip at the left edge. That opening frame MUST take whole rows of the focus's level, its edges in the gaps between them, and end on the right in the gap before the next column. A box of another branch that its top or bottom edge crosses MUST be drawn faded, at the context opacity, so the frame shows nothing cut but the parent's strip; once the person zooms or pans, every box is drawn as it is. The camera's zoom limits MUST let it frame the deepest leaf of a large product, which is very small against the product's box (`LA-EXP-DS06`), and fit the whole map in a phone's pane: 64 times the map's units at most, a ten-thousandth at least. The framed levels MUST fit the pane, however small their labels then are on screen; the depth decides only what is framed. The camera MUST move there from the view as it is, including one the person zoomed or panned, in one smooth zoom and pan (zooming out only as far as the pan needs) on the shared motion (`--motion-speed`, `--motion-ease`, at most twice the speed for a long path); on a page's first picture, on a resize and under reduced motion it MUST go there at once. Free zoom and pan move the same camera: the wheel and a pinch zoom about the pointer, a drag pans, and the zoom buttons zoom about the pane's middle; a gesture during a glide takes over from it, and the frame button and the `.` command frame the focus again.

The map MUST be drawn on a canvas, anew for each frame of the camera. A viewport MUST be kept in doubles, and every map point placed on screen in doubles relative to the camera's center, with no transform but the screen's pixel ratio, so a box deep in a large map is as steady at a deep zoom as at the top. Each label's lines MUST be drawn at their size in the map times the zoom, so text is crisp at any zoom whatever the map's range. A visually hidden layer of the drawn boxes, in the keyboard's order, MUST carry focus, Tab, the arrow keys, Enter and Escape, and each box's role and name for assistive technology, and the box it focuses is drawn with the focus ring. The pointer MUST find the box under it from the map's own outlines (a box's rectangle, a shape's polygon or rounded corners, a Voronoi cell's polygon), the last drawn first, so a child drawn over its parent is found before it.

title: Links are dashed curves that never move anything
statement: With the Links switch on, the graph MUST add the records the focused record links to and from, one hop, with the relation filters applied, and the links between them and the focus, drawn as dashed curves in their own color (`--link-edge`) between their boxes. Each linked record is drawn wherever it sits in the map, whatever its size on screen, and keeps its own place there: links never move anything. A linked record off screen MUST be counted by the edge hint on its side (`LA-V93-R18`). With it off, the graph MUST draw no cross-links. Trace mode stays for a whole chain.

title: A step that fulfills a requirement is traced with its flow
statement: Where a flow step fulfills a requirement or rule, the trace MUST show the step's flow too, so the rule is traced to the flow through the step.

title: Depth frames levels of the nav's tree below the focus
statement: The graph view of `/<record-id>` (`?view=graph`, or its graph pane beside others) MUST show the one map of the nav's tree, stages and folders included (see LA-EXP-DS04, LA-EXP-DS05), and at depth N (1 by default, up to 3) MUST frame the record, its parent at the left edge and its descendants down to N levels below it (see LA-EXP-DS09), with no cross-links: at depth 1 its parent (or folder) and its children (or their folders). A Links switch beside Depth, off by default, MUST add the record's own links, one hop (see LA-EXP-SP05). `/graph` on its own MUST open the first product.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Clicking a node re-centers the graph and changes the address
statement: Clicking a record node MUST re-center the graph on that record and change the address to its graph page, so the browser's Back button walks back along the path. A breadcrumb trail MUST show the records and groups visited, named as LA-V93-R34 says, and going back to one of them MUST cut the trail there.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Node and line style show kind, relation, errors and gaps
statement: Nodes MUST be colored by their stage, each of the five stages its own color, structure nodes their own and shaped by kind (see LA-V93-R06), a domain drawn as a hexagon (see LA-V93-R05), lines MUST be styled by relation, and records with errors or coverage gaps MUST carry a visible mark. A legend MUST explain the styles.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Kinds and relations can be switched off
statement: The reader MUST be able to hide and show each kind and each relation, and MUST be able to keep only the design and proof links (fulfills, invokes, happens in, and parent links to implementations and tests) in one step.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: The graph works from the keyboard
statement: Tab and Shift+Tab MUST move between the drawn nodes, Enter MUST focus the record or group with keyboard focus, and Escape MUST clear the filters and trace mode. Keyboard focus MUST always be visible.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: The graph is one map in columns that follow the parent/child tree
statement: The graph MUST be laid out left to right in columns by depth in the parent/child tree, one map for the product's tree (see LA-EXP-DS05): the product furthest left, then each level in its own column; the focus's ancestors to its left and its descendants to its right. Every record with the same parent, record or group, MUST sit in the same column whatever its kind (see LA-EXP-DS05). Parent/child lines MUST be drawn as the solid spine of the tree, passing through a group in its own column where the parent's children are grouped (see LA-EXP-UC04), and every other relation as a lighter, dashed cross-link. Links MUST NOT move anything: a linked record keeps its place in the map.
