In trace mode the graph MUST read left to right in its own columns: the requirement or rule, what fulfills it, the components, the tests, then the files.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Focusing moves the camera, not the map
statement: When the person focuses a record or group, the map MUST hold still: no node moves or changes size, and the camera glides, in one smooth zoom and pan on the shared motion, to frame the new focus and the levels the depth shows below it (see LA-EXP-DS09). The first picture of a page appears at once. When the system asks for reduced motion, nothing MUST animate: the camera jumps to frame the focus (see LA-V93-R01).
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Hovering a node spotlights it and what it joins
statement: Hovering or keyboard-focusing a node MUST brighten it, its lines and the nodes it joins directly, and dim the rest a step; leaving MUST restore the picture. It MUST change with the motion tokens, and at once under reduced motion.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Edge hints count the linked records past each edge
statement: With the Links switch on, at each canvas edge a small chip MUST count the records the focus links to that lie past that edge ("3 ↑", "8 →"), update as the camera moves, and hide when nothing is past it. Clicking a chip MUST glide the camera, at its zoom, to bring the nearest of them into view, without changing the focus.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: The arrow keys step out to the parent, in to a child and across
statement: While the graph has focus (after a click on its canvas or a box, in the Tree, Nested and Voronoi views alike), the plain arrow keys MUST step through the tree, each step moving the graph's focus: Left to the parent, Right to the first child, Up and Down to the previous and next sibling in the nav's order. From a box, keyboard focus follows. The arrow keys MUST never act while a text field has focus, nor with a modifier held. The steps MUST be listed in the shortcuts sheet, with buttons that carry tooltips and `aria-keyshortcuts`; no page-wide shortcut steps.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: A minimap shows the whole map and where the view sits
statement: A Minimap switch under Filters, off by default and kept per tab, MUST show a minimap in a corner: a true overview of the one map, its upper levels as boxes (as many as stay readable), the focus solid and the camera's view outlined as it moves, colored through the theme's tokens.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: A Tree, Nested or Voronoi switch shows parents beside their children or made of them
statement: The graph's toolbar MUST offer a Layout switch of Tree, Nested and Voronoi, Tree by default, kept with the tab's graph settings (never in the address), with a command and its shortcut (`v`, which steps to the next layout) in the command list. Tree draws the one map as an icicle, each parent beside its children (`LA-EXP-DS05`). Nested draws the same tree as boxes inside boxes: the product made of its domains, a domain of Define and Design, a stage of its folders, a folder of its records (`LA-EXP-DS07`), explored by the same camera (`LA-EXP-DS09`). Voronoi draws it as polygon cells inside cells (`LA-V93-R22`). Depth 1 to 3 frames the Tree view; the Nested and Voronoi cameras frame the focus's box or cell, so they have none, and there the Depth buttons are neither shown nor reachable, though they keep their place (`LA-EXP-DS09`). Everything else the graph does MUST work the same in all three: a click, Enter or a tap to focus, the hover spotlight with Details following it, the arrow keys stepping through the tree, Tab through the drawn boxes with a visible focus ring, `.` to frame the focus again, Links, Filters (a hidden kind keeps its space), trace mode, the fit and zoom buttons, the minimap, the trail, Back and Forward with the camera's glide, the side bar's Details, Outline and History, the problem and coverage marks, and the same roles and accessible names.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: The Voronoi view shows each parent as a polygon cell made of its children's cells
statement: The Voronoi layout MUST draw the focus's product as a hexagon split into polygon cells, one per domain, each domain's cell split into Define and Design, and so on down to the records, sibling cells of equal area with the same text, each showing its own name (`LA-EXP-DS08`), so the shape of a product can be compared with its Tree and Nested pictures. It MUST share the Nested view's camera, level of detail and keyboard order (`LA-EXP-DS09`), every drawn cell showing its label inside it at the text size it shares with its siblings (`LA-EXP-DS06`, `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12`), and it MUST never keep the page waiting while it is laid out: the layout runs off the main thread, and the canvas fills once it is ready.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Folders and records with several kinds of children are reached through one group each
statement: The graph MUST draw the nav's stages and folders as group nodes, and when a record's children, or a folder's records, include more than one kind the nav lists side by side, MUST put a group node per kind between them, labeled with the kind's plural label and the number of members, such as "Use cases (5)". A group MUST be drawn like a folder, differently from records. The parent/child spine MUST run record, group, record, while every cross-link (satisfies, proves and so on) MUST still run record to record. Every group is a level for the depth. Hiding a kind hides its kind groups (a stage or named folder has no kind of its own), hiding the parent/child relation hides every group, and trace mode MUST show no groups.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: A group shows its name and count, and clicking it goes to its address
statement: A group MUST show its name and count. Every member is always in the map, so there is nothing to open or fold in place, and a group has no chevron or other control of its own. Clicking the group, or pressing Enter on it, MUST go to its address, as clicking a record does.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: A group has its own address and can be the center
statement: A group MUST be the focus at its own address: a stage or folder at `/<domain-id>/<stage>[/<folder>]`, for example `/TL-LEND/define/use-cases`, and a kind group at `/<parent-id>/<kind>`. At depth 1 the camera MUST frame its parent at the left edge and all its members to the right, and depth counts levels from it as from a record. Its side bar names the parent and lists every member. The focused record's side bar MUST link to its groups. The breadcrumb trail and the browser's Back button MUST work for groups as for records. An address for a group that does not exist MUST say so.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: A group carries a mark when anything inside it has problems or gaps
statement: A group MUST carry the error, warning and coverage-gap marks that records carry whenever any member, or any record beneath a member, has them, so a group whose members are too small to draw still shows where the trouble is. The legend MUST explain groups and their marks.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: Groups take their own column between a parent and its children
statement: A group MUST sit in its own column, one after its parent's and one before its members', so the graph still reads left to right. A group's siblings, and the records at the same depth under other parents, share that column.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: Domain events sit under their aggregate, and their links are dashed and labeled
statement: In the graph, an aggregate's domain events MUST sit under it through a "Domain events" group, by the one-kind rule, and each event MUST be drawn as a flag in the spark colors. With the Links switch on, the `raises` links into an event and the `hears` links of the policies that hear it MUST be drawn dashed in spark and labeled with their relations' labels ("Reacts to", "Raised by"); with it off they are not drawn.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: A parent is as tall as its children, so the tree reads like an icicle
statement: In the map, a record, stage, folder or group MUST be as tall as its children stacked, each an equal part of it, and each child MUST sit right beside it, joined by a short, level parent line, so the tree reads like an icicle and no lines fan out from a parent to its children (see LA-EXP-DS05). Every node in a depth column MUST share the column's width, a fixed fraction of the map that shrinks toward the leaves, and siblings MUST share one text size, in proportion to their column's width or as large as every sibling's whole label allows, centered, the title wrapped on whole words (see LA-EXP-DS06). No node's size ever depends on what is in focus.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: The graph shows pattern rules under their pattern and follows as a cross-link
statement: In the graph a pattern's rules MUST sit one column to its right, under it, and a use case's `follows` link MUST be drawn as a cross-link, in its own line style named in the legend; a use case reached from the pattern by that link sits one column after it. …showing its pattern rule tests in every domain that follows it.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: In the graph a flow step sits under its flow
statement: In the graph a flow step MUST sit one column to the right of its flow, joined to it by the parent line, and, as for other children, MUST reach them through a group only when the flow also has children of another kind.
group_name: Read a flow step by step

title: A trace shows the fulfilling step, its flow and the components it uses
statement: Trace mode for a UC requirement MUST show each flow step that fulfills it, the flow the step belongs to, and the command or query the step invokes with its handler, with the step between its flow and those components.
group_name: Read a flow step by step

title: The graph reaches components and tests through the same groups
statement: In the graph a domain MUST reach its technical records and its tests through their stage and kind groups, as the nav does, and each record keeps its own place in the map (DS05)
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: The graph trail names what was visited
statement: The graph's trail of visited records MUST show a record as its title with its ID in parentheses, such as "Exploring (LA-EXP)", and a group by its name alone, without a count, such as "Use cases", naming its parent in its tooltip and accessible name. A long name MUST be cut short with an ellipsis, with the full text in its tooltip, and the current item MUST stay bold.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: Trace mode shows only the traceability chain and its files
statement: In trace mode the graph MUST show only the obligation, what designs it (for a UC requirement, the flow steps that fulfill it, the commands and queries they invoke and the views they happen in), the technical records that implement those, the tests under it, and the files those technical records and tests name.
group_name: Traceability

title: Trace mode is offered only for obligations
statement: The trace mode switch MUST be offered when the focused record is an obligation, and MUST NOT be offered for any other kind.
group_name: Traceability

title: The graph draws standards with a ruler
statement: The graph MUST draw a standard and its rules in the technical specification stage's color, shaped as a pattern and a pattern rule with a ruler mark (`LA-V93-R06`), and a `meets` link as a design line, and its key MUST say so.

title: Another domain's aggregate is a faded gray box labeled with its domain
statement: In an ERD the current domain's aggregates and entities MUST be drawn in the domain model stage's colors, and an aggregate of another domain MUST be a closed box, gray and faded, labeled with its domain.

title: A domain's ERD draws its aggregates as boundaries around their entities
statement: On a domain the Model view MUST draw each of its aggregates as a boundary containing its entities, the root marked, each entity with its fields: each field's name and type (a basic type, a value object's name, or "→ Aggregate" for a reference). It MUST draw a has one or has many line between entities, with crow's-foot ends, and a dashed reference-by-ID line from an entity holding a field typed by another aggregate to that aggregate's root (see LA-EXP-DS11); a referenced aggregate of another domain MUST be a faded box labeled with its domain. The Model view MUST draw nothing but entities, aggregates and these lines: no command, domain event, policy, specification, read model or query.
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: An aggregate's ERD draws its entities with the aggregates around it faded
statement: On an aggregate the Model view MUST draw its boundary with its entities, their fields and their has one and has many lines, and the aggregates it references, or that reference it, as closed boxes faded around it, joined by dashed reference-by-ID lines from the entity holding the field to the referenced aggregate's root.
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: An entity's ERD is its aggregate's, with the entity picked out
statement: On an entity the Model view MUST draw its aggregate's ERD with the entity highlighted.
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: Boxes lead to their pages, and a key lists what the diagram draws
statement: Clicking a box, or pressing Enter on it, MUST go to its page, keeping the open views, and a box MUST show a hover state; the highlighted entity on its own page leads nowhere. A key under the diagram MUST list only what the diagram draws, from: entity, root entity, aggregate boundary, has one, has many, reference by ID and other domain, with the highlighted entity and the faded aggregates when they are drawn. In a narrow pane the key MUST fold into a Key button.
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: The ERD fades the aggregates around it and its opening frame fits every box
statement: On an aggregate's ERD the aggregates it references, or that reference it, MUST appear faded, out of focus and out of the keyboard order, with their lines faded; on a domain's ERD other domains' aggregates MUST be faded too. The opening frame MUST fit every box, faded ones included, inside a margin at any window size, and edge hints MUST count the boxes past each edge (see LA-EXP-DS09).
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: The side bar never repeats what the page shows
statement: What the side bar shows MUST earn its place: no list or fact the main view already shows beside it (a record's children, its problems, its links grouped by label in the wiki's Traceability). It describes what the main view does not: the node under the pointer or selected, the file behind the page, the page's outline, and the file's history.

title: The side bar describes the focused record
statement: The side bar MUST show the focused record's kind, title, the opening of its text, its problems and coverage gaps, the records it connects to, and an "Open page" link to the record's address, `/<id>`.

title: The side bar folds away
statement: A record, group, product or domain page MUST have three columns: the nav, the main view and the side bar, with the views Details, Outline and History (`LA-EXP-UC12`). One side bar MUST serve the page in every view, and show nothing the main view already shows beside it (`LA-V95-R01`). It MUST fold away with a toggle in the page bar and a shortcut, remember that per view mode and per tab (`LA-V95-R05`), give its space to the main view, and on a narrow screen open as a bottom sheet that takes focus, keeps it inside, and closes with Escape (`LA-V61-R20`).

title: One side bar with three views, chosen from a switcher at its top
statement: The page's last column MUST be one side bar with a switcher at its top of three icon buttons, Details, Outline and History, each with `aria-pressed` and a tooltip, in a group labeled "Side bar views". The view shown MUST have a heading naming it and be the region the switcher's buttons control. Switching MUST keep keyboard focus on the button pressed and announce the view. The side bar keeps its width handle, its toggle in the page bar and its shortcut (`LA-V95-R03`).
group_name: Use the side bar for details, outline and history

title: The side bar keeps its open state and view per view mode and per tab
statement: The side bar's view mode MUST be the Wiki view when only the wiki is open, and otherwise the Graph or Model view open beside it. Each mode MUST keep whether the side bar is open and which view it shows, per tab (`LA-EXP-UC10`) across a reload, and as last used for a space's first tab. Until the Reader chooses, it MUST be closed in the Wiki view and open on Details in the Graph and Model views. On a phone it MUST stay a bottom sheet (`LA-V61-R20`) with the same three views.
group_name: Use the side bar for details, outline and history

title: Details follows the pointer and the selection, and repeats nothing the page shows
statement: In the Graph and Model views Details MUST show the node under the pointer or keyboard focus (the graph's spotlight), else the one selected by a tap, else the page's record: its kind, title and ID, its columns, data file and parent, its problems, and a compact Traceability in the relations' labels (`LA-V92-R07`), with Open for any other record and, in the desktop app, Reveal and Open in editor. In the Graph view it also lists what the graph connects to the center. In the Wiki view Details MUST show a record row that has focus or was right-clicked the same way, and otherwise only what the page leaves out: the data file and line, the columns of its row and the raw links both ways, plus a product's or domain's parent, children and problems, which its overview does not list.
group_name: Use the side bar for details, outline and history

title: Outline lists what the main view holds, as rows to jump to
statement: In the Wiki view Outline MUST list the page's sections and headings (Traceability and its groups, children, problems, the headings in its text) in page order and indented by level; a click MUST scroll the wiki to that heading, and the section in view MUST be marked (`aria-current="location"`) as the wiki scrolls. In the Graph view it MUST list the records the camera frames, grouped by level from left to right; in the Model view the diagram's boxes, those in focus first. Every list MUST be rows that are clickable anywhere (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R05`) and searchable past ten rows (`LA-V92-R20`).
group_name: Use the side bar for details, outline and history

title: History lists the commits that changed the record's rows, with what each changed
statement: History MUST list the commits that changed the selected record's rows (or the page's record's) in the data files, newest first, each with its date, author, subject and short hash, twenty at a time with "Load more". Changes in the working tree not committed yet MUST come first, labeled "Not committed". Each commit MUST show what it changed in the record's rows, the fields before and after, marked with the theme's tokens. When the product folder is not a git repository, or git is missing, it MUST say so calmly, as a hint, not an error. A group has no rows of its own, and says so.
group_name: Use the side bar for details, outline and history

title: Switching the side bar's view or what it describes moves nothing outside it
statement: Switching between Details, Outline and History, and Details following the pointer or the selection, MUST change only the side bar's content: the nav, the panes, their bars and titles, the canvas, the side bar's own box and its switcher MUST hold still (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R08`). A hover MUST redraw only the side bar, never the canvas.
group_name: Use the side bar for details, outline and history

title: Every page opens the graph in its Graph view, not from the nav
statement: Every record, group, product and domain page MUST open its graph in its own Graph view (the Graph view toggle in the page bar, Ctrl+G or Alt+G, Ctrl+2 and the command palette). The side navigation MUST NOT have a Graph item, open or as a rail: the graph is a view of a page, not a place of its own.

title: The graph is a component that any page can host
statement: The graph MUST be a component that takes its focus (a record ID, or a parent ID and kind) and reports every move to a new center through a callback, without reading or changing the address itself, so a page can show it in a pane beside the record page. Its links MUST still carry a real address so they open in a new tab. It MUST fill the width and height its container gives it and frame the focus again when that size changes.

title: A record or group has one address, whatever the view
statement: A record MUST be shown at its bare ID (`/<id>`), a product and a domain included, and a group of the graph's tree at its place in it: a stage or folder at `/<domain-id>/<stage>/<folder>` (a test-plan group's parts after it, `/<domain-id>/design/test-plan`), a record's kind group at `/<parent-id>/<kind>`, in every view.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: Wiki, Graph and Model are panes toggled on and off, named in the address
statement: A record, group, product or domain page MUST show its open views as panes side by side, always in the order Wiki, Graph, Model, as editor groups in VS Code. Wiki, Graph and Model MUST be on/off toggles, `aria-pressed` icon buttons in the View group at the right of the page bar above the panes; Model MUST be offered only on a domain, aggregate or entity page. At least one view MUST stay open: turning off the last open view MUST do nothing, and its toggle's tooltip MUST say so. Each pane's slim header MUST name its view at its left (its icon and "Wiki", "Graph" or "Model"), with, at its right, a button that closes the pane when more than one is open and its full screen button. There MUST be no Split mode and no Open beside button. The toggles and buttons MUST have a visible focus ring and their shortcut in their tooltip. The page's title MUST sit at the top of the leftmost open pane. The open views MUST be remembered between visits (local storage) and written to the address as `?view=` and their names, such as `?view=wiki,graph`, so a shared link opens as it was seen. Switching views MUST NOT lose keyboard focus: the toggles stay where they are, and when the focused element goes away with its pane, focus MUST move to the toggle of the view just switched. On a phone one view MUST show at a time (`LA-V61-R18`).
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: Every gap between panes resizes them, and any pane can be shown alone
statement: Every gap between two open panes MUST be a handle that resizes the two panes beside it. Each pane MUST have a full screen button, and Ctrl+3 MUST show only the focused pane (the leftmost, when focus is in none), like VS Code's maximize editor group; Ctrl+3 again, Escape or the same button MUST return to the panes, with focus back on the button.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: Both panes follow one focus, and Back and Forward move both
statement: Clicking a record in the graph MUST change the address, so the wiki pane and the side bar follow; following a link in the wiki MUST re-center the graph. Back and Forward MUST move both panes. The graph's depth, filters, open groups and trace mode MUST survive moving between pages and switching views.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: A group has a simple wiki page
statement: A group's wiki page MUST show its parent (as a link), its kind (with the kind's description), and its members as a list, each with its coverage marks and problem badge.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: Product and domain pages have the same views
statement: A product's and a domain's overview pages MUST offer the Wiki and Graph views, and a domain's the Model view too; their graph MUST be centered on the product or the domain.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: The title above a graph or a model keeps one height
statement: When the page's title sits at the top of a graph or a model pane, it MUST keep one fixed height whatever the record, each line cut with an ellipsis and the whole title in its tooltip, so the canvas below never moves when the focus changes. In the wiki pane the title MAY wrap.
group_name: Read a record as a wiki page, a graph or a model, side by side

title: A plain open uses the preview tab, or activates the page's open tab
statement: Opening a page by a plain click (a record link, a graph node or box, the nav, quick find, or Back and Forward) MUST open it in the preview tab, whose title is italic, replacing that tab's page in place; with no preview tab, a new one MUST open after the active tab. A page already open in a tab MUST activate that tab instead, as it was. Cmd- or Ctrl-click and middle-click on a link MUST still open a new browser tab.
group_name: Keep several records open in tabs

title: A tab is kept by double-click, the Keep open command or switching its views
statement: The preview tab MUST become a lasting tab, which the next plain open no longer replaces, when the reader double-clicks it, runs the "Keep the tab open" command (`keepTab`: Ctrl+K then Enter on a Mac, as in VS Code, and Alt+K then Enter elsewhere, where Ctrl+K is quick open), or opens or closes one of its views.
group_name: Keep several records open in tabs

title: A tab closes by its button, a middle-click or Alt+Shift+W
statement: Each tab MUST have a close button, shown on hover, on focus and on the active tab. Middle-clicking a tab MUST close it, and Alt+Shift+W (`closeTab`) MUST close the active tab; never Ctrl+W, which toggles the Wiki view on a Mac and closes the browser tab elsewhere. Closing the active tab MUST activate its neighbor to the right, or else to the left, and move the address there.
group_name: Keep several records open in tabs

title: Ctrl+Tab cycles the tabs, and the strip works as a tab list
statement: Ctrl+Tab (`nextTab`) and Ctrl+Shift+Tab (`previousTab`) MUST activate the next and previous tab in tab order, wrapping at the ends, and with the other tab commands MUST be listed in the shortcuts sheet and the palette, their keys in tooltips and `aria-keyshortcuts`. The strip MUST be a `tablist` of `tab` elements with `aria-selected`, only the active tab in the Tab order; with a tab focused, the arrow keys, Home and End MUST move between tabs, Enter or Space MUST activate the focused one and Delete MUST close it.
group_name: Keep several records open in tabs

title: Each tab keeps its own views, pane sizes, wiki scroll and graph settings
statement: Each tab MUST keep its own open views, pane sizes, wiki scroll position and graph settings (depth, trace, filters, open groups), and activating it MUST bring them back. A new tab MUST start from the active tab's views, sizes and settings, at the top of the page; a link that names views opens a new tab in those.
group_name: Keep several records open in tabs

title: Tabs are kept per space for the session and come back on reload
statement: The open tabs, their order, which one is the preview and which is active, and each tab's state MUST be kept per space for the browser session; switching spaces MUST swap the tab set for that space's own. Reloading MUST bring back the same tabs, the same active tab and each tab's views. A saved tab or space's last page that is not a page's address MUST be dropped.
group_name: Keep several records open in tabs

title: The tab strip leads the page bar, each tab with ID and title
statement: The tab strip MUST sit at the left of the page bar above the panes, apart from the panes' own headers, which name their views. Each tab MUST show its record's ID in mono and its title, cut short with an ellipsis, with both in full in its tooltip; a group's tab MUST show its label ("Use cases (7)"). Tabs that do not fit MUST scroll sideways by wheel or trackpad, and the active tab MUST scroll into view; the page bar keeps its height. On a phone the tabs MUST fold into an "Open pages" button in the page bar that opens them as a sheet (`LA-V61-R21`).
group_name: Keep several records open in tabs

title: Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch record tabs in the desktop app
statement: View › Tabs MUST offer Show Next Tab, Show Previous Tab, Keep Tab Open and Close Tab, running `nextTab`, `previousTab`, `keepTab` and `closeTab` by command ID. Show Next Tab and Show Previous Tab MUST own Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab as their accelerators, since a web page never receives those keys; the other two MUST take no key from the app.
group_name: Keep several records open in tabs

title: The Model view is offered on domain, aggregate and entity pages only
statement: A domain, aggregate or entity page MUST offer a Model view, a pane toggled like Wiki and Graph and sitting after them. Any other page MUST NOT offer it, and an address that names it there MUST show the page's other named views.

title: The products page is the space chooser
statement: The products page (`/`), the rail's home and the only page of the specs outside every space, MUST list each product with its name and domain count, and nothing from inside the products: no problems and no coverage.
